title: Keying service audit schema and archival retention guidelines
content:
Purpose and scope

This doc defines the audit/event schema and archival/retention guidelines for the Keying Service (KMS/HSM/BYOK) and describes how evidence is packaged and exported to SIEMs. It covers integration points with RBAC v2, operational rotation procedures (scheduled and emergency), and recommended encryption-at-rest patterns for multi-tenant storage. Audience: security, compliance, SRE, platform engineering, and third-party auditors.

Design objectives and constraints
- Provide a compact, consistent audit schema that supports: compliance evidence extraction, incident reconstruction, and automated SIEM ingestion.
- Ensure minimal PII/secret leakage in logs; all secret materials (DEKs, plaintext keys) are never logged.
- Enable long-term retention of signed evidence artifacts (manifests + hashes) while keeping access controls auditable.
- Support both Redwood-hosted keys and customer-supplied BYOK (HSM-backed) with clear onboarding, proof-of-possession, and rotation semantics.

High-level architecture (textual)
- Keying Service API layer (auth + RBAC v2) -> KMS controller (envelope handling, key versioning) -> HSM cluster manager (BYOK HSM connectors) -> audit collector -> evidence packager -> archival store (S3-like, immutable prefixes) -> SIEM export bridge (supports ECS/JSON and CEF).

Audit event schema (core fields)
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC timestamp when the event was emitted
- event_id: stable UUIDv4 for the audit event
- service: string, e.g., "keying-service" or "hsm-connector"
- component: service sub-component, e.g., "api", "kms-controller", "hsm-client"
- action: high-level action, e.g., "key.create", "key.rotate", "key.export_attempt", "key.onboard.byok", "hsm.authenticate", "evidence.package", "siem.export"
- actor_id: subject who performed the action (user email, service principal), redacted if PII-sensitive per policy
- actor_type: one of ["user", "service", "automation"]
- target_type: one of ["key", "key_version", "secret_store", "tenant_config"]
- target_id: opaque identifier for the target (key id or version id)
- key_metadata: stringified tags/labels (no secret material)
- outcome: one of ["success", "failure", "partial"]
- reason: short human-readable code or message when outcome != success
- request_id: correlation id propagated across the request path
- ip: origin IP (if available and permitted by privacy rules)
- rbac_evidence: array of role/grant snapshots relevant to permission check at time of action (store role ids, not full policy blobs)
- signature: base64 representation when event is signed by the collector (used for immutable evidence)

Notes on sensitive fields: actor_id and ip are subject to privacy rules: store only hashed versions or tokenized references when required by privacy jurisdiction. Key material MUST NEVER appear in any log field. key_metadata must not include plaintext key material.

Example audit event (single-line JSON)
{
  "timestamp": "2025-06-12T18:42:03Z",
  "event_id": "3f2b9d6e-7a4a-48a5-9c2a-0f4f3d9a1c2b",
  "service": "keying-service",
  "component": "kms-controller",
  "action": "key.rotate",
  "actor_id": "svc-deploy@redwood.com",
  "actor_type": "service",
  "target_type": "key",
  "target_id": "key-tenant-1234:version-2025-06-12-v2",
  "key_metadata": "tenant=tenant-1234;purpose=db-encryption",
  "outcome": "success",
  "request_id": "req-6b8c9a2f",
  "rbac_evidence": ["role:tenant-admin"],
  "signature": "MEUCIQD...base64sig..."
}

Evidence packaging and archival pipeline
- Trigger points for evidence packaging: any key lifecycle event (create/rotate/revoke/export), periodic snapshots (daily), and forensic captures on incident.
- Package contents: list of audit events (JSONL), manifest.json with SHA256 hashes, a signed manifest (collector HSM-signed), and metadata.json (retention tags, legal hold flags, tenant id).
- Storage model: immutable prefixes in archival bucket with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) and object lock (where supported). Example prefix: archives/tenant-1234/2025/06/12/pack-3f2b9d6e/
- Access controls: ACLs limited to security/audit roles; retrieval requires two-step approval (automation ticket + human approver) for >7yr artifacts.
- Evidence signing: the collector service signs the manifest using a dedicated evidence signing key (stored in HSM). Signatures are verified by auditors during retrieval.

Retention policy and export windows (recommended)
- Short-term operational logs (audit stream): 1 year online hot storage (ECS/ELK), 90 days for full raw event retention in high-cardinality indices.
- Medium-term evidence packages: 3 years in archival bucket (quick retrieval within 24 hours).
- Long-term compliance archive: 7 years immutable with legal hold support for regulated customers (optionally longer for specific contracts).
- Deletion: automatic tombstone + secure purge job that overwrites object metadata and then deletes only after legal hold clearance.

SIEM export mapping and formats
- Supported formats: Elastic Common Schema (ECS/JSON), CEF (for legacy collectors), and compact JSONL for S3 ingestion.
- Recommended export fields to SIEM: timestamp, event_id, service, component, action, actor_type, actor_id_hash, target_type, target_id, outcome, reason, request_id, tenant_id, rbac_snapshot_id.
- Rate/volume control: export bridge batches events into payloads up to 10k events or 10MB and throttles per-tenant to avoid noisy-tenant floods.
- Example Elastic mapping: event.dataset: keying-service.audit, event.kind: event, event.action: key.rotate, user.id: hashed(actor_id), ecs.version: 8.12

RBAC v2 integration notes
- Every permission check emits an rbac_check event with: check_id, actor_id, resource_id, permission, decision, roles_considered.
- rbac_evidence snapshots in core audit events should reference a small set of role ids + timestamp. Full role definitions are stored in a separate immutable reference table (retained 3 years).
- Principle of least privilege: service tokens used for automation are scoped narrowly and carry minimum roles; any escalation must be recorded as an audit event with approval metadata.

Key rotation procedures (procedural guidance)
- Scheduled rotation (recommended cadence): DEKs rotate monthly, KEKs rotate annually unless customer contract requires different cadence. Use versioned key IDs and keep old DEKs until all dependent ciphertexts are rewrapped or marked for lazy rewrap.
- Automated rotation flow: 1) create new key version (inactive), 2) test decrypt/reencrypt on sample objects in canary tenant, 3) flag new version active, 4) background rewrap workers process data per tenant or lazy rewrap on-access with versioned metadata, 5) retire old key version after rewrap completion and retention period.
- Emergency compromise flow: 1) immediate revoke of affected key versions in KMS (deny decrypt/unwrap), 2) issue incident id and add legal hold to related evidence, 3) take forensic snapshot (evidence package) and replicate to offline archive, 4) engage customer (for BYOK) and rotate KEK with out-of-band verification, 5) run rewrap or data recovery plan.
- Test rotation play: run quarterly simulated rotation on non-prod tenants with full evidence capture and SIEM trace to validate end-to-end auditability.

BYOK and HSM-specific guidance
- BYOK onboarding checklist: customer provides key handle or public key, vendor performs proof-of-possession (challenge-response) and returns attest to customer, record HSM slot id and attestation in onboarding manifest, set tenant-byok flag and store only references (no private key material).
- HSM connectors: connector logs must include connector_id, hsm_fingerprint, session_id, action, and outcome. Connectors must push tamper-evident event streams to the collector.
- Attestations: store HSM attestation certificates alongside evidence packages to prove hardware origin and firmware versions at time of events.

Encryption-at-rest patterns and recommendations
- Envelope encryption (recommended): DEK per object, KEK per tenant; store object.ciphertext + metadata {key_id, key_version}. DEKs are ephemeral and never leave KMS unencrypted.
- Database encryption: column-level encryption with DEKs derived from tenant KDK where high-performance required; use field-level tokenization for PII.
- Object storage: use SSE-KMS for service-managed objects; for tenant BYOK, wrap object DEKs with customer KEK before storing.
- Disk-level: only used for ephemeral compute nodes. Use LUKS/BitLocker with keys wrapped by KMS, do not rely on disk encryption as sole control for long-term data.
- Key derivation: use HKDF with tenant-specific salt when deterministic keys are required (e.g., per-tenant deterministic IDs), avoid storing derived keys.

Operational controls and checks
- Daily smoke checks: collector health, signature verification pass rate, evidence packaging latency
- Weekly audits: sample evidence packages validated by security and compliance (manifest hashes vs archive)
- Monthly metrics: unhandled failures in export bridge, SIEM ingest failure rate, retention-schedule drift
- Access reviews: quarterly review of who can retrieve long-term archives; maintain two-person access approval for >1yr artifacts.

Appendix: quick checklists
- Onboard BYOK: verify PoP challenge, record attestation, create tenant mapping entry, schedule rotation cadence, set monitoring alerts.
- Rotate KEK (scheduled): create new key version (inactive), run canary decrypt tests, promote new version, start background rewrap, publish rotation audit events.
- Compromise emergency: revoke key, create evidence package, legal hold archive, notify stakeholders, begin rewrap/migration.

Open questions and TODOs
- Decide standard retention for hashed actor_id across EU vs US customers (privacy trade-offs).
- Archive retrieval SLA for compliance audits (default 48 hours vs expedited 4 hours for enterprise contracts).
- Implementation: map rbac_evidence references to existing RBAC v2 role id format and add schema docs for role snapshots.
